newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Peru coffee exporters sees crop up 10 pct in 97/98.
newsitem.headline: Peru coffee exporters sees crop up 10 pct in 97/98.

text.p: The Peruvian coffee crop is expected to increase by 10 percent in 1997/98, a senior official with Peru's exporters' association, the Camara Peruana de Cafe, said on Wednesday.
"We expect to see an increase in the crop of about 10 percent, up from last season," Eduardo Montauban Urriaga told Reuters at a coffee and tea conference in Vienna.
Camara Peruana de Cafe handles 80 percent of Peru's total coffee exports.
Urriaga said Peru's 96/97 crop, which ended in March, totalled about 100,000 tonnes, of which 91,181 were exported.
He said 25 percent of exports went to Korea and Japan, 45 percent to Europe, while the remaining 30 percent largely went to the United States.
He said high coffee prices on global markets and good weather in recent months had boosted production prospects.
Urriaga said Peru had between 400,000 and 500,000 60-kg bags of high-quality mild washed arabica coffee in stock, adding that Peru and Ecuador were the only two countries with stocks.
